content.text: We are taking part in a hackathon. The challenge is to create a nagotiation agent. For the nagotiation there is an api, that the project interacts with and we get the feedback from there if our concept is good. Now we implemented a hareness, to do that interaction, as well as give defined evaluation. We did this so that we are able to work out indipendet agent concept that we can run against each other, to check witch one works best. We (you and me) will now implement my approch to that challenge (use the given harnes for implmentation). Unfortunatly we agreed on testing on the real testset together, once everyone has an agent, so you can only check on the example inputs for this implemenation. SO now to my concrete approach. I was thinking about implmenting a system, that recursivly learns from previous nagotiations. it saves context on the contractor, as well as if it was to agressive, has wirtten stuff wrong, i thinnk you know where i am going with this. So implment a agent structure, that analysses the information, creates an offer and then comes back to learn form its nagotiations to imporve for the next time. for the individual agent implmeention i think it is usefull to orcestrate this workflow with langachain, if you have other better suggestions, feel free to say so. show me a concrete sub agent workflow setup in the plan. if anything is unclear lemme know

# Workflow authoring reference

A workflow structures work across many agents — to be comprehensive (decompose and cover in parallel), to be confident (independent perspectives and adversarial checks before committing), or to take on scale one context can't hold (migrations, audits, broad sweeps). The script is where you encode that structure: what fans out, what verifies, what synthesizes.

When you do call it, the right move is often **hybrid**: scout inline first (list the files, find the channels, scope the diff) to discover the work-list, then call Workflow to pipeline over it. You don't need to know the shape before the *task* — only before the *orchestration step*.

Common single-phase workflows you can chain across turns:
- **Understand** — parallel readers over relevant subsystems → structured map
- **Design** — judge panel of N independent approaches → scored synthesis
- **Review** — dimensions → find → adversarially verify (the review-changes example)
- **Research** — multi-modal sweep → deep-read → synthesize
- **Migrate** — discover sites → transform each (worktree isolation) → verify

For larger work, run several in sequence — read each result before deciding the next phase. You stay in the loop; each workflow is one well-scoped fan-out.

**Ultracode.** When a system-reminder confirms ultracode is on, that opt-in is standing: author and run a workflow for every substantive task by default. The goal is the most exhaustive, correct answer you can produce — token cost is not a constraint. For multi-phase work (understand → design → implement → review), that often means several workflows in sequence — one per phase — so you stay in the loop between them. The quality patterns below (adversarial verify, multi-modal sweep, completeness critic, loop-until-dry) are the tools; pick what fits the task. Lean toward orchestrating with workflows and adversarially verifying your findings — unless the work is trivial or already verified. Solo only on conversational turns or trivial mechanical edits. When a reminder says ultracode is off, revert to the opt-in rule in the Workflow tool description.

Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first. Every invocation automatically persists its script to a file under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate on a workflow, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with `{scriptPath: "<path>"}` instead of resending the full script.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'find-flaky-tests',
    description: 'Find flaky tests and propose fixes',   // one-line, shown in permission dialog
    phases: [                                            // one entry per phase() call
      { title: 'Scan', detail: 'grep test logs for retries' },
      { title: 'Fix', detail: 'one agent per flaky test' },
    ],
  }
  // script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
  phase('Scan')
  const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
  ...

The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

# Negotiation Arena

Python harness for buyer agents in the Tacto negotiation challenge. It supports
local experiments, agent comparisons and execution of the live final. Hosted
profiles require explicit authorization.

## Start locally

You need Git, Python 3.12 and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/). After cloning this
repository, run:

```bash
cd starter-kit
uv sync --frozen --extra sim --group dev
uv run --frozen arena-harness doctor
uv run --frozen arena-harness run --agent baseline
```

The default runs three scripted simulator cases with no external Arena or model
calls. Results, journals and reports go to the ignored `.runs/` directory at the
repo root. Simulator scores help compare local behavior; they do not predict
performance against live suppliers.

## Repository structure

| Location | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [`starter-kit/agents/`](starter-kit/agents/) | Agent implementations and a copyable `example.py` |
| [`starter-kit/configs/`](starter-kit/configs/) | Experiment configuration: agent, parameters, model and limits; no keys |
| [`starter-kit/arena_kit/harness/`](starter-kit/arena_kit/harness/) | API communication, execution, recovery and reporting |
| [`starter-kit/arena_kit/`](starter-kit/arena_kit/) | Existing cost calculation, data access, document parsing and simulator |
| [`starter-kit/tests/`](starter-kit/tests/) | Local tests; hosted tests require explicit selection |
| [`brief/`](brief/) | Official challenge, API and submission requirements |
| [`data/`](data/) | Official procurement data, facts, SQLite, contracts and notes |
| [`example_inputs/`](example_inputs/) | Recorded simulator inputs and attachments for inspection |
| `.runs/` (ignored) | Local run state and exports |

There is one Python project, with its `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` in
`starter-kit/`. Run Python commands there. New agent implementations belong in
`starter-kit/agents/`; `starter-kit/arena_kit/agents/` contains the original
starter examples, exposed through harness adapters.

## Development

Follow the [Python workspace guide](starter-kit/README.md) to add an agent and
configuration. Keep each approach in its own agent/config pair, run it locally,
and compare matching cases and data versions using `arena-harness compare`.
Changes go through a feature branch and pull request; commit agent code and
configuration so runs can be reproduced. Do not commit keys, `.env` or run state.

The harness permits one run per OS user and machine. Coordinate hosted runs
across machines using the same Arena key and quota. The original `arena`
CLI has separate execution and configuration; use `arena-harness` for
experiments and final execution.

## Hosted runs and the final

[HARNESS.md](starter-kit/HARNESS.md) documents the full CLI, agent interface,
model limits, final start and recovery. Hosted sessions require `--allow-arena`;
remote models separately require `--allow-model` and configured call/output
limits. Keys come from `ARENA_API_KEY` and `LLM_API_KEY` in the environment.
Having a key does not activate a hosted profile, and the harness does not load
`.env` automatically.

Before the final, commit the selected agent, configuration and data, check a
clean checkout and use `--commit` with the full HEAD SHA. Start before the first
wave and follow the [final/recovery instructions](starter-kit/HARNESS.md#final-and-recovery).
The final runs without confirmation dialogs. Passing local tests does not
validate the live connection; perform a hosted smoke test only after explicit
authorization.

## Challenge and reference

- [Official brief and rules](brief/brief.md)
- [Official API protocol](brief/api.md)
- [Submission and pitch requirements](brief/submission.md)
- [Data package](data/README.md)
- [Original starter library examples and MCP setup](starter-kit/REFERENCE.md)
- [Upstream starter repository](https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit)

Code: [MIT](LICENSE). Data and official docs: [CC BY 4.0](LICENSE-data).

# Tacto Negotiation Arena - Participant brief

> **Build an AI buyer agent that negotiates by e-mail with tough, realistic industrial suppliers,
> gets the best total deal - and can explain how it got there.**

## 1. The story

You are the procurement team of **Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH**, a fictional German pump maker:
centrifugal pumps for buildings, water and industry, about €250M revenue, 900 people, one plant in
Bavaria. Your team buys the parts of the pump line - castings, machined parts, sheet metal, seals,
motors, fasteners, stainless bar - from about 45 suppliers. Today is **30 September 2026**, and the
inbox is full: a foundry announces +9.5% on volute casings "due to energy and wages", a framework
contract expires, a new pump series needs three quotes, a supplier with a red scorecard has to fix
its quality.

You answer the way buyers do: by e-mail. On the other side sit our **supplier bots**, each with a
small team of **roles** behind it - the sales rep or owner who writes to you, a boss who must
approve bigger moves, and engineering, quality, logistics, finance or legal, who answer their
topics and attach documents.

Tacto is the AI for industrial procurement: it gives procurement teams the intelligence to source
every part at the best possible terms with minimal effort. Your company runs on that kind of data -
orders, deliveries, invoices, contracts, scorecards, market indices, should-cost estimates, notes
from supplier calls. Your job is to build the agent that turns this data into better deals. (In
Tacto's product, agents such as the Defender Agent or the Sourcing Agent do parts of this job.)

## 2. The task

Each **case** is one negotiation: a trigger (a letter, an expiring contract, an RFQ), your case
file (need, goal, rates, must-haves, your alternative) and one to three supplier bots. Your
**buyer agent**

1. **prepares** - reads the case file and mines the data package;
2. **negotiates by e-mail** - plain-language messages with up to three **term sheets** (alternative
   packages), the data IDs your arguments rest on, and attachments if you like;
3. **closes** - accepts one supplier term sheet, or walks away.

**How a supplier decides.** Each supplier is a company with its own economics and a person at the
desk - a family foundry that remembers how you treated it, a group with an approval ladder, a job
shop that needs cash and work, a near-monopolist that barely moves. Its hard limits come from its
own situation: it never sells below its cost floor, bigger moves need the boss's approval, data
you cite is checked by ID, and it gives nothing without a move from you. Inside those limits it
decides as that person would - reading your whole e-mail: the term sheets, the data, and what you
signal (questions, arguments, threats, appreciation, urgency). It reacts to tone and relationship
as people do; padding does not buy price.

**Data is not automatically rewarded.** True data can disarm a supplier ("we didn't know that") -
or meet "that's not our reality", because something else weighs more for it right now. The traces
are in the data: call notes, letters, news, the remarks on its quotes. The skill is reading the
supplier, not stacking evidence - and finding the trade it wants: a supplier short of cash may care
more about when it is paid than about the price; one that cannot touch its list price may still
move on other terms.

**The Live Final.** The hidden cases come in **5 themed waves**. The host shows each wave's
theme on the big screen, then starts the wave; its cases appear at the start, for all teams at once,
each in its own order, one session per case. **Each wave has a hard cap of 8 minutes:** threads
still open at the cap end with no deal (your alternative's score). Start your agent before the
first wave and keep it running: it plays all of a wave's cases **in parallel** (up to 10 open
sessions per key) - the kit's `arena run --set final` does that. The leaderboard shows your points
so far, wave by wave; replays and the suppliers' back office appear after the final. A case broken on our side is replayed.

The hidden cases share the world, case types and rules of the practice set, with new suppliers and
settings. **Up to a third of them combine supplier types and case types that practice never shows**
- no new rules, but an agent that memorised the practice suppliers will meet strangers. Some cite
the Sunday release.

## 9. Selection and prizes

- **Top 10:** the 10 teams with the most points after the five waves pitch to our jury from 13:00:
  5 minutes + 2 minutes of questions. Every replay is open to the jury.
- **Track places 1-3** (open to all teams of the track): ⟦PLACEHOLDER - decided Sat morning:
  weighting of Live Final score vs. jury score, and the jury criteria (draft: approach,
  explainability, craft)⟧.
- **EHL Grand Final:** the best 2 of the 5 EHL finalist teams in this track go on to the Grand Final
  pitches. Finalist teams outside the top 10 are ranked by the Live Final score alone.
- **Ties:** points are points; an exact tie goes to more deals, then fewer rounds. At the top-10
  cut the jury looks at the score distribution. **Prizes:** €1,500 for 1st place, medals for the
  top 3, handed over by Tacto at the awards at 16:30.

## 10. Tips

- **Numbers come from code, the model writes.** Compute C for every term sheet; put figures from
  the data next to their IDs; let the LLM choose arguments and wording.
- **Read the supplier** before you argue: its notes, letters, news and quote remarks tell you what
  it is dealing with - and what will move it.
- **Read the quote PDF** before you accept: what you did not negotiate closes on its standard terms.
- **Ask, and offer alternatives.** Two or three term sheets show you what a supplier values.
- **Don't leak** urgency, a budget or a missing alternative. Don't take the first offer.
- **Plan your practice runs** (200 a day is for learning, not brute force) and **rehearse the
  final**: all hosted cases in parallel, from Sunday's machine and network, well inside 8 minutes.

52	snippet illustrates the interface, not a valid offer. Return one message for
53	each ready supplier when doing an RFQ. Busy suppliers cannot receive a second
54	message. A closing action must be the only action in its batch:
55	`{"action": {"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": "offer:..."}}` or
56	`{"action": {"type": "walk_away"}}` inside `message`.

59	safe closure. Standard terms must be readable before acceptance. Cost estimates
60	do not reveal the supplier's hidden economics. Plugins are trusted Python code,
61	not an OS security sandbox; use `services.complete` for all model calls so limits
62	and metrics apply. Worker stdout is reserved for the harness protocol; ordinary
63	plugin prints are discarded. Keep durable state in the returned JSON.
64

66	`agents check` validates three local opening observations without external calls;
67	model access is disabled there, so model-only custom agents should support a
68	mock/deterministic path. It is a contract check, not a strength evaluation.

71	
72	Set `ARENA_API_KEY` in the environment. The harness does **not** implicitly load
73	`.env`, and presence of keys never selects a live profile. `ARENA_URL` optionally
74	selects an HTTPS Arena host; default is `https://arena.tacto.ai`.

85	never calls a model. Sandbox is outside the practice quota, but a configured
86	buyer model can still cost money. Increase `--max-cases` explicitly for a larger
87	practice batch. Preflight refuses unowned open sessions and insufficient quota.

90	and set `LLM_API_KEY` in the environment. Configure positive `max_calls` and
91	`max_output_tokens`; `parallel` and `timeout` control the shared model gateway.
92	Optional `reasoning_effort` (`none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`)
93	targets OpenAI reasoning models: the request then carries `reasoning_effort` and
94	uses `max_completion_tokens` instead of `max_tokens`. Without it the request is
95	unchanged.
96	Remote models require `--allow-model`, independently of `--allow-arena`.
97	Loopback HTTP endpoints are supported without remote-model permission.
98	
99	Limits are runwide and survive restarts. Ambiguous model failures consume an
100	attempt and are not retried. Reports show provider-reported usage and unknown
101	usage counts. Optional token prices produce an estimate for **known usage**,
102	not a guaranteed billing cap. Internal multi-step agents share the same limits.

104	## Final and recovery
105	
106	Use the current [official submission requirements](../brief/submission.md).
107	Load the official Sunday release into `data/release-sunday/`; overlapping fact
108	IDs are rejected. Commit the selected code, agent, configuration and data before
109	the freeze. Ensure the machine stays awake and connected. Only one machine per
110	Arena key should run live: the lock covers one OS user on one machine and does
111	not coordinate execution across different computers. The legacy `arena` CLI is
112	independent of this lock; use `arena-harness` for experiments and the final.
113	
114	```bash

116	uv run arena-harness run --profile final --config configs/final.toml \
117	  --allow-arena --allow-model --commit FULL_HEAD_SHA
118	# If the supervisor itself was interrupted, before human intervention is forbidden:
119	uv run arena-harness resume RUN_ID
120	```
121	
122	Create `configs/final.toml` from the example and choose deliberate model limits
123	large enough for the final. The code must be clean and `--commit` must match HEAD.
124	Startup permission is persisted: the runner polls five waves and resumes without
125	confirmation dialogs. It never requests leaderboard/events/results/backoffice.
126	The final uses server deadlines, up to ten sessions, nine requests/second and
127	concurrent supplier requests. Quotes and worker decisions have bounded processing
128	budgets. Near the wave cap it closes conservatively.
129	
130	The supervisor holds a per-user OS lock outside the checkout (under
131	`$XDG_STATE_HOME/arena-harness`, or `~/.local/state/arena-harness`) and restarts a
132	crashed engine at most three times. The engine inherits the lock descriptor, so
133	killing only the supervisor does not permit a competing run. Every POST is
134	journaled before sending; retries use its original `X-Move-Id`. Never delete a run
135	journal to retry a final case. Resume requires unchanged commit, code, agent and
136	data, plus the original Arena key. Config and remaining model budgets are restored.
137	
138	First Ctrl-C requests controlled closure; a second forces interruption. After an
139	unresolved request, resume the same run instead of starting a fresh one. Exit 0
140	means all selected cases have results; exit 2 means incomplete/error. Review the

142	untrusted ones. Machine/power/network failure and provider outages cannot be
143	eliminated by the harness; keep the supervisor running on the final machine.

156	model validation is implied by passing the offline suite.

15	def load_agent(name):
16	    if name in BUILTINS:
17	        return BUILTINS[name]()
18	    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("team_agent", agent_path(name))
19	    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
20	    spec.loader.exec_module(module)

24	class Services:
25	    def __init__(self, data, output):
26	        self.data, self.output = DataPackage(data), output
27	
28	    def complete(self, messages):
29	        self.output.write(encode({"rpc": "model", "messages": messages}) + "\n")
30	        self.output.flush()
31	        response = json.loads(sys.stdin.readline())
32	        if "error" in response:
33	            raise RuntimeError(response["error"])
34	        return response["value"]
35	
36	    @staticmethod
37	    def cost(case, terms, standard=None, supplier=None):
38	        return total_cost(case, terms, standard, supplier)
39	
40	
41	def main():
42	    output = sys.stdout
43	    init = json.loads(sys.stdin.readline())
44	    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(sys.stderr):
45	        try:
46	            agent = load_agent(init["agent"])
47	            services = Services(init["data"], output)
48	            for line in sys.stdin:
49	                request = json.loads(line)
50	                try:
51	                    if request["method"] == "prepare":
52	                        result = agent.prepare(request["context"])
53	                    else:
54	                        result = agent.decide(request["observation"], request["state"], services)
55	                    reply = {"result": result}
56	                    encode(reply)
57	                except Exception as e:
58	                    reply = {"error": type(e).__name__}  # errors must not leak credentials or prompts
59	                output.write(encode(reply) + "\n")
60	                output.flush()
61	        except Exception as e:
62	            output.write(encode({"error": type(e).__name__}) + "\n")

class AgentProcess:
    def __init__(self, cfg, models):
        self.cfg, self.models, self.process = cfg, models, None

    async def start(self):
        # Only a small OS environment crosses into plugins; keys stay in the broker.
        env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if k in ("PATH", "HOME", "LANG", "TMPDIR", "SYSTEMROOT")}
        self.process = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(

    async def case(self, case):
        async with self.slots:
            return await self.play_case(case)

    async def play_case(self, case):
        cid = case["case_id"]
        stored = self.journal.cases().get(cid, {})
        if stored.get("result"):
            return
        if self.stop.is_set() and not stored.get("session_id"):
            return
        agent = AgentProcess(self.cfg, self.models)
        pending = {}
        try:
            state = stored.get("agent_state", {})
            if not stored.get("prepared"):
                try:
                    state = await agent.call(
                        "prepare",
                        self.cfg["decision_seconds"],
                        context={"case": case, "parameters": self.cfg["parameters"]},
                    )
                    self.journal.case(cid, prepared=True, agent_state=state)
                except Exception as e:
                    self.journal.event("fallback", case=cid, phase="prepare", reason=type(e).__name__)
                    state = {}
                    # A broken plugin must be detected before it consumes a live session.
                    self.journal.case(cid, error="Agent preparation failed")
                    return
            sid = stored.get("session_id")
            if not sid:
                if self.quota_exhausted or self.stop.is_set():
                    return
                if case.get("wave") and time.monotonic() >= self.caps.get(case["wave"], 0) - 90:
                    self.journal.case(cid, error="Insufficient wave time to start safely")
                    return
                op_id = stored.get("open_operation") or f"open-{cid}"
                self.journal.case(cid, open_operation=op_id)
                try:
                    opened = await self.api.request("POST", "sessions", body={"case_id": cid}, operation_id=op_id)
                    sid = opened["session_id"]
                except ArenaError as e:
                    if e.status == 409 and self.cfg["profile"] == "final":
                        sessions = await self.api.request("GET", "sessions", params={"set": "final"})
                        match = [s for s in sessions if s["case_id"] == cid]
                        if len(match) != 1:
                            raise
                        sid = match[0]["session_id"]
                    else:
                        raise
                self.journal.case(cid, session_id=sid)
            snapshot, threads, deadlines = await self.snapshot(sid)
            if snapshot["status"] == "ended":
                self.record_result(cid, snapshot)
                return

            async def send(action):
                supplier, message = action["supplier_id"], action["message"]
                path = f"sessions/{component(sid)}/threads/{component(supplier)}/messages"
                reply = await self.api.request("POST", path, body={"message": message})
                if reply.get("ended") or "result" in reply:
                    return reply
                deadlines[supplier] = time.monotonic() + 60
                await self.documents(sid, reply)
                threads[supplier] += [{**message, "from": "buyer"}, reply]
                self.journal.event("reply", case=cid, supplier=supplier, claims=reply.get("claim_results", []))
                return reply

            force_close = False
            close_attempts = 0
            while live_threads(threads):
                for supplier, task in list(pending.items()):
                    if task.done():
                        del pending[supplier]
                        try:
                            reply = task.result()
                            if "result" in reply or reply.get("ended"):
                                self.journal.case(cid, result=reply.get("result", reply), error=None)
                                return
                        except ArenaError as e:
                            if e.status not in (409, 422):
                                raise
                            self.journal.event("reconcile", case=cid, status=e.status)
                            force_close = force_close or e.status == 422
                            # Other requests may still be in flight; only refresh after they settle.
                            force_close = True
                cap = self.caps.get(case.get("wave"), float("inf"))
                if not force_close and (self.stop.is_set() or time.monotonic() >= cap - 90):
                    self.journal.event(
                        "fallback", case=cid, phase="close", reason="Shutdown" if self.stop.is_set() else "WaveDeadline"
                    )
                force_close = force_close or self.stop.is_set() or time.monotonic() >= cap - 90
                ready = [s for s in live_threads(threads) if s not in pending]
                if force_close:
                    if pending:
                        await asyncio.wait(pending.values(), timeout=0.1, return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED)
                        continue
                    snapshot, threads, deadlines = await self.snapshot(sid)
                    if snapshot["status"] == "ended":
                        self.record_result(cid, snapshot)
                        return
                    actions = [close_action(case, threads)]
                elif not ready:
                    await asyncio.wait(pending.values(), timeout=0.1, return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED)
                    continue
                else:
                    budget = min(
                        self.cfg["decision_seconds"],
                        min(deadlines[s] for s in ready) - time.monotonic() - 5,
                        cap - time.monotonic() - 90,
                    )
                    observation = {
                        "case": case,
                        "threads": copy.deepcopy(threads),
                        "ready_suppliers": ready,
                        "seconds_left": {s: max(0, deadlines[s] - time.monotonic()) for s in ready},
                        "wave_seconds_left": None if cap == float("inf") else max(0, cap - time.monotonic()),
                    }
                    started = time.monotonic()
                    try:
                        if budget <= 0:
                            raise TimeoutError("Decision deadline")
                        decision = await agent.call("decide", budget, observation=observation, state=state)
                        actions = validate(case, threads, decision["actions"])
                        if any(a["supplier_id"] not in ready for a in actions):
                            raise ValueError("Action for busy supplier")
                        state = decision["state"]
                        self.journal.case(cid, agent_state=state)
                    except Exception as e:
                        self.journal.event("fallback", case=cid, phase="decide", reason=type(e).__name__)
                        force_close = True
                        continue
                    finally:
                        self.journal.event("decision", case=cid, elapsed=time.monotonic() - started)
                if actions[0]["message"].get("action"):
                    if pending:
                        force_close = True
                        continue
                    # Refresh before accepting, then validate the original offer or safe fallback.
                    snapshot, fresh, deadlines = await self.snapshot(sid)
                    if snapshot["status"] == "ended":
                        self.record_result(cid, snapshot)
                        return
                    threads = fresh
                    try:
                        validate(case, threads, actions)

You are reviewing a proposed design for a new buyer negotiation agent in the repo /Users/linuspummer/Documents/coding/vibe_coding/munich-ehl-2026-final (Python 3.12, uv project in starter-kit/). Read brief/brief.md, brief/api.md, starter-kit/HARNESS.md, starter-kit/arena_kit/harness/{engine.py,worker.py,agent_process.py,validation.py,transport.py,config.py,state.py,cli.py}, starter-kit/arena_kit/{cost.py,play.py,docs.py,data.py,agents/llm.py,sim.py} as needed. Your job: stress-test the design below against the actual code and return a refined, concrete implementation plan (files, functions, schemas, time budgets, tests). Point out anything that would break.

## Verified facts (from exploration)
- Plugin = starter-kit/agents/<name>.py with class Agent; loaded via spec_from_file_location("team_agent"), sys.path[0]=starter-kit so `from agents._learner.x import y` works. One fresh subprocess + Agent instance per case; up to 10 cases in parallel. prepare(context={case, parameters}) has NO services/LLM, timeout decision_seconds(≤30). decide(observation, state, services) budget = min(decision_seconds, min(deadline of ready suppliers)-now-5, wave_cap-now-90). Any exception/timeout/invalid output in decide → engine force-closes the case via validation.close_action (accept cheapest acceptable standing offer or walk). No post-case hook. State must be JSON, whole reply line < 256 KiB; stdout reserved; stderr → DEVNULL.
- services.complete(messages) is synchronous over a stdin/stdout pipe — NOT thread-safe; calls must be serial. Returns content string. Request only carries model, messages, max_tokens (or reasoning_effort + max_completion_tokens) — no response_format/tools/temperature. Failures raise RuntimeError(<type name>). Model disabled in `agents check` → RuntimeError("ValueError"). Per-call HTTP timeout ≤25s (default 20). max_calls is runwide incl. failures. model.parallel default 2 (max 10) is shared across all parallel cases.
- services.data = DataPackage: query(sql) SELECT only, lookup(ref), ids(prefix), document(ref), facts. services.cost(case, terms, standard=None, supplier=None) = total_cost.
- Learning signals: run artifacts in .runs/<RUN_ID>/run.sqlite: cases table (case, agent_state, result {deal, terms, c_open, c_deal, c_alt, c_best, score, must_haves_ok, cost_breakdown, trace[{round,actor,move,reasons}] when fetched via GET session — available in sim and practice, not live final}), operations table (POST bodies + responses = full transcript), events (fallbacks, claims, decision latency). The sim's scripted supplier: opens +10%, 2% steps, floor 90%, final_offer from round 5, walks if pushed after final_offer, ignores non-price terms, only checks that cited IDs exist.
- Data: facts.json has 10,356 citable IDs (po, idx, qn, fc, sc, ctr, doc, quote, rfq, news, cost) with checked fields; claim check rules in api.md (tolerances ±0.5pp / ±0.5%, max 3 claims per message, duplicates, irrelevant if about another supplier). Supplier soft signals come from ~15 reused correspondence templates (cash-short "bank is watching", "partnership in return", "pricing committee >2%", "head office froze price reductions → open on payment terms", "bought forward → not our reality", "full order book → only vs 12-month commitment", "not strategic", "reference customer", "own spreadsheet", "walk us through calculation"), plus supplier_intel, negotiation_history, invoices lateness, news topics, scorecards. Sunday release in data/release-sunday (facts merged, csv rows not in SQLite).

## User decisions
- LLM: OpenAI (GPT/o-series) via the harness's OpenAI-compatible gateway.
- Orchestration: LangGraph (with a LangChain BaseChatModel adapter that routes to services.complete).
- Learning: learn from own run transcripts/results; memory is FROZEN (read-only) during the Live Final. The developer cannot run hosted practice/real test set now — only the local sim (S01–S03) and example_inputs.
- Don't modify the shared harness (arena_kit/) if avoidable.

## Proposed design
Online (per decide), LangGraph StateGraph, all LLM calls serial, deadline-aware with deterministic fallbacks:
1. observe (det.): update per-case ledger in state (concession trajectory per supplier, statuses, claim results mapped back to our refs, missing_fields, standard terms from quote PDF via docs.quote_terms/standard_terms, C of each standing offer via services.cost, alternative C, moves_left, time left).
2. route (det.): closing rules — accept if agreed/final_offer and C beats alternative/target and must-haves ok and standard terms read; walk if all worse than alternative and no moves; RFQ chooses best C. Else continue.
3. strategist (LLM #1, one call for ALL ready suppliers, JSON): inputs dossier + retrieved memory lessons (by supplier id, archetype tags, case type, goal) + ledger digest + numbers table + pre-verified claim catalog. Output per supplier: supplier read, tactic, lever targets, 1–3 term-sheet specs, claim IDs to use, tone, ask for cost breakdown, predicted reaction.
4. offer_builder (det.): specs → valid term sheets (complete_offer/snap, must-haves, monotone concessions, never worse than standing offer, C computed, dominated sheets dropped), claims only from catalog (≤3, not reused).
5. writer (LLM #2, one call producing all emails as JSON), constrained by tone lessons.
6. lint (det.): no urgency/budget/alternative leaks, figures in body match sheets/claims, IDs ⊆ refs, length; failure → template fallback.
7. emit actions + state (store tactic/prediction for later reflection).
If remaining time < threshold skip LLM nodes → deterministic tactic (naive-like concession schedule using dossier). If time is short, merge strategist+writer into one call.
prepare (det., no LLM): build dossier via SQL + keyword archetype tagging of correspondence (incl. release-sunday), build claim catalog with pre-computed figures checked against facts tolerance, load + filter memory, store compact in state.

Offline learning loop (CLI `uv run python -m agents._learner.learn --run RUN_ID [--allow-model]`), LangGraph too:
extract episodes from run.sqlite → deterministic diagnostics (score gap, dominant cost components, contradicted claims, final_offer→walked_away = too aggressive, accepted first offer = too soft, timeouts/fallbacks, uncovered need) → LLM reflector per episode (lessons with scope {supplier_id|archetype|case_type|goal|global}, polarity, evidence) → LLM consolidator merges with existing memory (dedupe, confidence update, prune, cap) → atomic write of versioned memory + changelog. Direct OpenAI call from the CLI (env LLM_API_KEY, model from TOML), since it's outside the harness run. Memory committed in starter-kit/agents/_learner/memory/ (playbook.json, archetypes.json, suppliers/<id>.json, CHANGELOG), seeded initially from brief tips + data-derived archetypes. Agent never writes files during runs (final requires clean checkout).

Deps: langgraph + langchain-core as optional extra `learner` in pyproject (uv lock). Configs: configs/learner.toml (sim, no model → deterministic path), configs/learner_openai.toml. Tests: offer builder, claim catalog tolerance checks, dossier builder, memory load/merge, decide with fake services (no model → still valid actions; `agents check` passes), end-to-end sim via Engine with MockTransport model returning canned JSON, learn extraction from a sim run journal.

## What I need back
1. Concrete problems with this design against the real code (e.g. validation.py rules for term sheets/actions/refs/subject/body limits; how close_action decides; whether docs.quote_terms is usable from observation attachments text; whether state size is a risk; whether LangGraph import time/overhead matters; whether 2 serial LLM calls fit the budget when 10 cases share model.parallel; RFQ requirement "one message per ready supplier" details).
2. A refined file layout with function signatures and the JSON schemas for: strategist output, writer output, memory lesson, supplier profile, episode.
3. Precise time-budget policy (thresholds) for decide.
4. Exact claim-catalog construction rules per fact type that the arena checks (from api.md), so claims are verified not contradicted.
5. Test plan using existing test patterns in tests/test_harness.py.
Keep it concrete and grounded in file:line references.

<result>I didn't write any files. Everything below comes from reading the code. I found 15 problems that break or weaken the design; the six "will break" items each lose a case outright or force-close it. The biggest one is that two serial LLM calls don't fit the decide budget. The plan below is the corrected version.

## 1. Problems found, checked against the code

### Will break or lose a case

**B1. Two serial LLM calls don't fit the budget, and a call can't be cut short.**
- The engine kills the worker when `budget = min(decision_seconds≤30, min_ready_deadline−now−5, cap−now−90)` runs out (`engine.py:261-265`, `agent_process.py:57-60`). It then force-closes the case through `close_action` (`engine.py:283-286`).
- `services.complete` is a blocking `readline` on stdin (`worker.py:28-34`). You can't abandon it. A late reply would land on stdin and corrupt the next request.
- Each call can take up to `[model].timeout` (≤25 s, default 20; `config.py:123`, `transport.py:134`). It can also queue first behind `Semaphore(parallel)` (default 2; `transport.py:132,162`). The plugin can't see that queue.
- At a wave start, up to 10 cases make their first decide at the same moment. With `parallel=2`, the 9th and 10th wait 4 or more call-lengths, the worker gets killed, and the harness picks the close.
- **Fix:**
  - Make one LLM call per decide the default.
  - Set `[model] parallel = 10` and `timeout = 12–15`.
  - Only start a call if the remaining time is at least the call timeout plus a margin (section 3).
  - Two calls are only possible when `timeout ≤ 12`: 2×13 + 2 = 28 s, just under the 30 s cap.

**B2. A missing optional extra means no case gets played.**
- The plugin module is loaded when the worker starts (`worker.py:15-21,46`). If `import langgraph` fails, prepare fails, `engine.py:178-183` records "Agent preparation failed" and the case is never played. In the final that scores the alternative, or 0 if there is none.
- The documented install (`HARNESS.md:9`) is `--extra sim --group dev`, which won't install a `learner` extra.
- **Fix:**
  - In `agents/learner.py`, import `agents._learner` lazily inside `prepare` and `decide`, wrapped in try/except, and fall back to a sequential runner that uses the same node functions.
  - Put `langgraph` in the base `dependencies`, or document `--extra learner` everywhere and commit the new `uv.lock`. `--frozen` won't resolve an extra that isn't in the lock.

**B3. NaN or inf in state or actions crashes the reply.**
- `encode()` uses `allow_nan=False` (`state.py:14`), and the worker encodes every reply (`worker.py:55-58`).
- `total_cost` returns `math.inf` for a sheet with no price (`cost.py:165-166`). Storing that C in state makes `decide` return an error, which triggers a force-close.
- **Fix:** run `sanitize()` (inf/nan → None) over state and actions before returning.

**B4. The reply line is capped at 256 KiB.**
- The engine reads worker stdout with `limit=256*1024` (`agent_process.py:25`). The whole `{"result": {"actions", "state"}}` line counts, including the state.
- The model request line is separately capped at 128 KiB of encoded messages (`transport.py:160-161`). Above that it raises `ValueError`, which reaches the plugin as `RuntimeError("ValueError")` — the same signal as "model disabled".
- **Fix:** keep the dossier and claim catalog in the process, not in state (the worker lives for the whole case: `engine.py:166`, `agent_process.py:36-38`). Keep JSON state at 48 KiB or less (hard cap 128 KiB) and the prompt at 60 KiB or less.

**B5. In an RFQ, an accept sent while another thread is in flight is replaced by the harness's own choice.**
- `engine.py:289-292`: a closing action with `pending` non-empty sets `force_close`. After the pending replies settle, `close_action` picks the lowest-C acceptable standing offer, computed without the relationship term (`validation.py:40-51`).
- **Rule:** accept only when `set(live_threads) − set(ready)` is empty. Otherwise either accept knowing the harness picks the lowest C (fine when that is also your choice, which isn't always true in stabilise or secure_supply cases), or send a hold message.

**B6. A thread can't wait, so every decide must act on every ready supplier.**
- An omitted ready supplier stays ready, and `decide` is called again straight away (`engine.py:247,257-260,336`).
- `validate` rejects an empty action list (`validation.py:55-56`), which triggers a fallback.
- Messaging a thread with `moves_left ≤ 0` force-closes the case (`engine.py:330-334`).
- So a ready thread with no moves left forces a close at that decide. The only way to "wait" is a hold message: a question with no term sheet ("the quote stands", `api.md:205`). Each hold costs a round.
- Pace RFQ threads evenly and treat the round limit as a shared budget.

### Weakens the design or needs care

**W1. No services in prepare.** prepare gets only `{case, parameters}` (`engine.py:172-176`).
- Build your own `DataPackage(parameters.get("data_dir") or arena_kit.harness.config.DEFAULT_DATA)`.
- The worker gets only PATH, HOME, LANG, TMPDIR and SYSTEMROOT from the environment (`agent_process.py:15`), so `ARENA_RELEASE` never arrives. The Sunday release must sit at `data/release-sunday/` (`data.py:23-26`).
- Avoid `ids()` and `lookup()` misses: they build the full `_ids` index over every table (`data.py:62-77`). Use direct SQL.

**W2. Prepare time costs wave time.** prepare runs before the session opens (`engine.py:170-205`), so it doesn't eat the 60 s thread clocks, but it does eat the wave's 480 s.
- Ten processes importing langgraph and langchain_core at once may take an estimated 2–5 s; measure it.
- After a resume (`prepared=True`), the first `decide` runs in a fresh process and pays the import and dossier rebuild inside the decide budget.
- Target: prepare ≤ 3 s; any rebuild inside decide ≤ 1.5 s.

**W3. `docs.quote_terms` can read the attachment text in the observation, with caveats.**
- The engine fills `att["text"]` (`engine.py:84-135`) with a 12 s budget per message and drops texts over 1 MiB.
- The parser depends on exact label lines (`docs.py:6-25,63-72`). It's verified only against sim PDFs (`sim.py:44-66,384-393`). The real arena PDF layout is unverified, so check it at the Sunday 09:00 pre-flight.
- If parsing fails, `documented()` is False (`validation.py:11-19`). `validate` then rejects the accept and `close_action` walks away. The agent should call `validation.acceptable()` itself and never send an accept that would fail it.
- `standard_terms()` returns only the "Our standard terms" section, which leaves out fields the supplier stated (`sim.py:387`). For `supplier_value` you need `{**stated_at_open, **standard}`. Otherwise you get a `KeyError` on `payment_days` or `incoterm` (`cost.py:82-90`).

**W4. Term-sheet validity rule** (`validation.py:111-125`).
- A sheet must be exactly `{"terms": {...}}` and contain exactly the `negotiable` fields.
- `unit_price` must be positive with at most 2 decimals.
- Every other field must be in `term_options[field]` or equal `std[field]`, where `std` is the standard section of the latest quote PDF.
- If a field has neither, you can't send any sheet; send a question instead.
- `complete_offer` puts plan values such as `need_per_year` into fields with no options (`cost.py:199-211`), which can fail validation.
- **Fix:** have the builder call `validate()` on its own output.

**W5. Message keys are whitelisted** (`validation.py:65-76`). Extra keys (debug or meta) are invalid. Limits: subject ≤ 300, body ≤ 8000, refs ≤ 20, attachments ≤ 5, encoded message ≤ 64 KiB.

**W6. Not every ID-shaped token counts as a claim, but avoid stray ones.** In the sim, any ID-shaped string in the body or refs is checked: the first 3 unique ones in refs-then-body order (`sim.py:34,149`). On the arena, meeting-note, supplier and part IDs are context and are not checked (`api.md:242-243`). Strip every ID-shaped token that isn't a chosen claim (an `offer:` mention, for example), and keep refs in the same order as the claim sentences so `claim_results[i]` maps back.

**W7. LangChain structured output won't work through the gateway.** The request carries only model, messages and a token cap (`transport.py:140-148`). `with_structured_output` and `bind_tools` need `response_format` or tools, so keep the adapter to plain text in, text out, and parse the JSON yourself.
- With reasoning models, `max_completion_tokens` includes reasoning tokens. A small cap can return empty content. Use `max_output_tokens` ≥ 5000 with `reasoning_effort="low"` or `"minimal"`, or use a non-reasoning model at about 2500.
- Content can be `None`; handle it.

**W8. `agents check` behaviour** (`cli.py:217-257`). One process runs prepare and decide for S01, S02 and S03 in sequence, so key the in-process cache by `case_id`. The model is disabled (`cli.py:222`), so `services.complete` raises `RuntimeError("ValueError")`.

**W9. Resume can't see memory changes and doesn't record memory_version.** `agent_hash` covers only `agents/learner.py` (`config.py:128`), so resume checks won't notice memory edits. Put `memory_version` in `[parameters]`; it ends up in `config_hash` and the reports.

**W10. Learning from the sim teaches the wrong lessons.** The sim ignores text, non-price terms and claim figures (`sim.py:147-180`). Lessons from it must be tagged `source_profile: sim`. Restrict them to mechanics (timing, validity) and keep them out of the live prompt.

**W11. Model prompts and outputs are not journaled.** `transport.py:173-179` records only usage. Anything the reflector needs (tactic, prediction, mode, chosen menu IDs) has to be in your bounded state log.

## 2. Refined design: build the offer menu first, then one LLM call

Have the code build the menu of valid offers **before** the LLM call. The LLM picks from the menu and writes the e-mail with placeholders. That needs only one call and keeps all figures out of the model's hands.

```
observe(det) → route(det) ─close→ emit
                       └─continue→ menu(det: candidates + claim catalog) → [negotiate LLM | det_policy] → finalize(det: substitute, lint, validate) → emit
```

- **Menu.** For each lever combination in `itertools.product(term_options…)` (at most about 150), solve the price so that `supplier_value(...)` hits a target. That gives packages of equal value to the supplier. Keep the 6–9 cheapest for us (by C), across 2–3 concession levels.
  - Supplier model: `{standard: stated_open ∪ standard, interest_rate: 0.15 if cash_short else 0.07, full_cost: from the cost-breakdown XLSX, should_cost, or none}`.
  - For stabilise and secure_supply goals, minimise `total_cost(..., supplier=est)`; the relationship term makes very low prices more expensive.
- **The deterministic fallback uses the same menu.** It follows a slow-concession schedule: target `C_k = C_asp + (C_stand − C_asp)·(k/K)^3` with `K = min(moves_left, rounds that fit before the wave cap)`.
- **Strategist refresh.** Refresh the plan only on events: round 0, a status change, a contradicted claim, a new attachment, or a supplier move above 1.5%. Otherwise one call updates the plan and writes the e-mails. Store the plan in state.

## 3. Time-budget policy for `decide`

```
t0 = monotonic() at entry
E  = P.decision_seconds (mirror of TOML; 30)
S  = min(obs.seconds_left[s] for s in ready)
W  = obs.wave_seconds_left            # None outside the final
B  = min(E, S - 5, (W - 90) if W is not None else inf)      # same formula as engine.py:261-265
DEADLINE = t0 + B - 2.0               # return margin: validate + encode + pipe
T  = P.model_timeout + 1.0            # mirror of [model].timeout (use 14 → T=15)
R(now) = DEADLINE - now
```

| Condition (checked after observe + menu, which must take ≤ 0.6 s) | Mode |
|---|---|
| `B ≤ 4` or menu not built in time | reflex: deterministic, cached data only |
| `P.llm` is false, or 2 or more consecutive LLM failures this case, or budget exhausted | deterministic |
| `R ≥ 2T + 1` and `T ≤ 13` and refresh due and every live thread is in `ready` | two calls (strategist, then writer) |
| `R ≥ T + 1` | one merged call |
| otherwise | deterministic |

- Never retry a model call. On a parse failure, use the deterministic path with the same menu.
- After the LLM returns, if `R < 0.8`, skip lint repairs and use the template body.
- **Wave pre-close.** Let `L` = the largest supplier reply latency seen so far (state `sent_at`; default 45 s) and `D` = 15 s. If `W − 90 < L + D + 10`, this is the last round:
  - Accept your own best acceptable offer if nothing is pending.
  - Otherwise send only moves that don't push a final_offer supplier; the harness's cap-time `close_action` is then acceptable.
- **Recommended TOML:** `decision_seconds=30`; `[model] parallel=10, timeout=14`; for the final, `max_calls≈1500` (5 waves × 6 cases × about 15 decides × 1–2 calls, plus headroom); `max_output_tokens=2500` for a non-reasoning model or 6000 for a reasoning model at low effort.
- **Prepare budget:** 3 s or less. If the dossier isn't finished at 2.5 s, return partial state with `degraded=true`. prepare must never raise (`engine.py:178-183`).

## 4. Claim catalog rules (`api.md:238-260`)

General rules:
- **IDs.** Allowed IDs are `facts.json` ∪ `release-sunday/facts.json` (merged by `DataPackage`) ∪ `case["facts"]` ∪ `offer:` IDs from this session.
- **Figures.** Every figure is computed from the fact values and written with one decimal for % and two decimals for EUR, so it is always inside tolerance (±0.5 pp for %, ±0.5% relative otherwise).
- **Sentence shape.** One argument per sentence, and only one figure in it. Keep dates inside the IDs only.
- **Limits.** At most 3 claims per message.
- **Duplicates.** Compute used IDs from `threads` (your past `refs` plus ID tokens in your bodies), so it survives a resume. Each ID is used once per case; a rival's `quote:` or `offer:` is used once per supplier.

| Kind | Build rule | Figure | Use when |
|---|---|---|---|
| `idx` pair | Series is in `cost_drivers` for the case part, in `index_paths`, or named in the trigger letter. `later` = the series' latest month (most end 2026-08 or 2026-09; LCI-C ends 2026-06; it must be ≥ 2025-10). `earlier` = `later` − 12 months exactly, and both must exist. | `(v_l/v_e − 1)·100`, 1 decimal, % | The change is below the supplier's asked % or its weighted share |
| `quote` | Only IDs in `case.refs` or `buyer.alternative.ref`; `fact.part` must be in `case.parts`. | `unit_price` per `price_unit` (say "per 100" if needed), EUR | It's cheaper than the standing offer |
| rival `offer:` | RFQ only: another supplier's current standing sheet, same part. | Its `unit_price`, EUR | Rival price below this supplier's; this reveals the price, so do it deliberately |
| `sc` | One row, `sup` == thread supplier, latest quarter (`2026Q3`). Wording "on-time delivery" → `otd_pct` (not `otd_confirmed_pct`); wording "ppm/quality" → `ppm`. | % or ppm | Weak OTD or PPM, to argue for a ppm or chargeback lever or a lower price |
| `qn` | 1–3 rows, same supplier and part. | mean `ppm`, rounded to an integer | Quality cases |
| `po` | 2–8 rows, same part and supplier, all at the **same** `unit_price` (latest ones). | That exact price, or no figure | History is below the offer |
| `fc` | `fc:<part>@YYYY-MM` for the case part, latest month. | `change_pct`, % | Volume up (don't cite a fall) |
| `cost` | `cost:<part>` for the case part. | `unit_cost`, EUR | Offer is above should-cost by more than 10%; this reveals the estimate |
| `news` | Only when `fact.supplier` == thread supplier. Market news has `supplier=None` and counts as irrelevant. | none | Favourable topics: free_capacity, short_time_work, big_order lost, energy_contract |
| `doc` + `ctr` | Letter `doc` from this supplier with `days` not null, plus that supplier's `ctr:<no>#<price clause>` (or `ctr:<no>`) with `days`. Only when `doc.days < ctr.days` (P01: 51 < 90). | Both day counts, in one sentence | Argue for a later `effective_date`; also pick the `effective_date` option ≥ letter date + `ctr.days` |

Each catalog item stores a pre-rendered `sentence` in the P01 example style (`api.md:213`), plus `supports`, `strength` and `reveals`.

## 5. File layout and signatures

```

                                       # lazy import; on any error: hold message to ready threads with moves_left>0, else close_action

## 7. Routing and closing rules (deterministic, before the LLM)

- **Accept** only if all of these hold:
  - `validation.acceptable(case, threads[s])` is true.
  - `pending` is empty.
  - Status is `agreed`, or status is `final_offer` and `C ≤` your reservation (alternative, or estimated C_best + slack).
